svg.aria-label: torch.distributed.pipelining's chain protocol against the multi-consumer edge a block residual needs, with the five suggested interfaces
svg.text: torch.distributed.pipelining today: a chain. Block AttnRes: one output with many consumers. Five interfaces would close the gap.
outputs go to the NEXT stage only; gradients come from the NEXT stage only
fwd_cache / bwd_cache hold one stage's own inputs and outputs for one mb, for its own backward
nothing keeps a received activation for a LATER stage on the same rank
no notion of an output consumed by a non-adjacent stage; the chunk id stays inside the stage;
backward P2P buffers are sized from the next stage's input-gradient strides
backward_one_chunk is called in eval too (base class returns at once); every output is assumed to get a gradient
Block AttnRes: b0 committed at S0 is read by S1, S2, S3
the edge b0 -> {S1, S2, S3} does not exist in the chain protocol; the subclass builds it from the
chain: relay along the hops and keep what arrived (routing tables), deposit + collect on a rank
green: forward reads of b0 magenta: every consumer's gradient must reach S0, summed
same-rank consumer (S2 on R0): nothing travels, but the gradient still has to merge into S0's
-- the store deposit, collected before S0's backward, which the schedule orders last on the rank
The five interfaces, where each one sits

g.text: multi-consumer stage output: the library owns the routing table (per stage: commits, held on rank, carried by the hop); the relay + store is one implementation
rank-local delivery: a consumer on the producer's rank (interleaved) gets the tensor by reference; the schedule merges its gradient before the producer's backward
chunk id and lifecycle for the submodule: a context (current mb) plus callbacks at mb end and step end -- removes the wrappers, enables per-mb release
dense backward P2P buffers: empty(shape) receive + contiguous() send; stride-sized buffers fail when a stage starts with cat / stack / slice
forward-only and no-gradient contracts: backward_one_chunk under has_backward=False as part of the subclass contract; outputs with requires_grad=False get None

svg.text: Where they bite today: 1 and 2 are the whole adapter / subclass (BlockLayoutTables, RankStore, deposits); 3 is the two wrappers the first version needed;
4 is the _DenseGradient identity op in the model; 5 is the has_backward guard and the None-gradient payload under LoRA (2026-09-06).
torch's own fwd_cache / bwd_cache are not 1 or 2: they hold a stage's own inputs and outputs for its own backward, nothing across stages or ranks.
